correctness.rationale: The exact symmetric crossing set is bounded by the unique root \(c=(1-c)^{1+\ell}\). The escaping negative-side coordinate is \(z=g(x)\), with neutral update \(\phi(z)=z+z^{1+\ell}\); the boundary identity \(\phi(1-c)=1\) prevents skipped crossings. Thus the normalized Lebesgue survival law equals \(g^{-1}(\delta_{n-1})/c\) for every \(n\ge1\). The inverse-coordinate recurrence \(w_m=\delta_m^{-\ell}\) has increments \(\ell-\ell(1+\ell)/(2w_m)+O_\ell(w_m^{-2})\). Establishing \(w_m=\ell m+O_\ell(\log m)\) justifies summation and the absolutely convergent renormalized increments, which give a finite \(K_\ell\) and an \(O_\ell((\log m)/m)\) remainder. Taylor expansion of the inverse crossing map yields the three coefficients and the relative error \(O_\ell((\log n)^2/n^2+n^{-1/\ell})\). The restriction \(\ell<1\) makes its last component \(o(n^{-1})\). The accompanying finite threshold and coefficient checks corroborate, but are not used to prove, the infinite statements.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text comparisons distinguish the specific normalized-Lebesgue central first-return law and its relative \((\log n)/n\) and \(1/n\) coefficients from published leading invariant-induced-measure tail estimates. Coates–Luzzatto–Muhammad Propositions 2.6 and 3.5 establish leading decay with relative power errors for any exponent strictly less than one, which do not determine the \((\log n)/n\) coefficient. Bansard-Tresse–Freitas Proposition 4.4 recalls the leading induced tail. Muhammad–Schindler extends the class to regularly varying neutral behavior and leading tails, not this three-term Lebesgue return formula. Equation and parabolic-tail searches found no demonstrated equivalent. Unindexed general parabolic/renewal literature remains a real risk; search absence is not novelty proof.

value.rationale: The originating full-branch family is motivated by long intermittent excursions and power-law return distributions. The symmetric map makes the natural central crossing return distribution computable exactly at every integer, not just asymptotically. The exponent-determined, strictly positive coefficient of the relative \((\log n)/n\) correction, followed by a well-defined constant, quantifies the first finite-time deviation from published leading power laws. The section is fixed by the natural zero crossings rather than an arbitrary numerical cutoff. This precision is relevant to sharp renewal and survival calculations; the claim does not assert new global mixing bounds.
